title: Kernel Scouting Service: lightweight probe-driven kernel selection using arch signatures and seq-len forecasts
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Mixed prefill + decode workloads across heterogeneous GPU fleets show non-uniform tail latency. Static kernel selection (single kernel per model/arch) suffers when sequence length distribution shifts or when a hardware variant has divergent microbenchmark characteristics. We need a low-overhead, per-request scouting mechanism that: 1) fingerprints the request/arch shape, 2) runs O(1)-cost microprobes to estimate candidate kernel perf for current seq-len, and 3) picks the kernel with best expected latency/cost while preserving safety/fallback.

Proposal: Implement a Kernel Scouting Service (KSS) in the runtime control plane that attaches a lightweight probe step to the prefill handshake for a small fraction of warm requests, and maintains a per-(model,arch,seq-len-bucket) scouting table. Key features:
- Arch signature: compact fingerprint of GPU type, compute capability, memory bandwidth tier, and driver/version.
- Seq-len forecast: estimate likely decode token count from prompt metadata + historical session distribution to pick probe lengths.
- Microprobes: tiny timed kernels (one-shot) executed in isolated slots or on preemption-safe lanes to measure latency for candidate kernels. Probe budget configurable per-tenant to bound overhead.
- Online autotune loop: scouting table updates using exponential smoothing and weights recency. Contrasts historical aggregate scores with live microprobe samples to adapt to drift.
- Safety: fall back to conservative kernel if probe fails; limit probe frequency per model/tenant; ensure KV cache and memory usage unaffected.

Goals and metrics: reduce p99 prefill+decode latency for mixed-length workloads by >=15% vs current static defaults, with probe overhead <2% of total request time and no regression in mean latency. Maintain throughput and not reduce GPU utilization by >3% for production mixes.
acceptance_criteria: KSS integrated into runtime control plane and configurable via model config
Per-(model,arch,seq-len-bucket) scouting table persisted with TTL and exposed in console
Automated probe budget enforcement per tenant and global safety limits
Benchmark showing >=15% p99 improvement on mixed-prefill workloads in synthetic and replay tests
Probe overhead measured and demonstrated to be <2% on representative traffic
Graceful fallback path validated (no cache corruption, no memory leaks) and unit/integration tests added
milestones: Integration with model config and console flags (2025-11-21)
updates: 2025-11-03 - Triage: assigned to Marcus. Initial perf targets set after discussion with PM (Priya Desai).
2025-11-06 - Design review: PM asked for explicit tenant-level probe budget and opt-out. Decided to implement per-tenant caps and config flag. Action: add config schema and console toggle.

2025-11-10 - Prototype: implemented microprobe harness using isolated CUDA streams and lightweight timing; initial probes show stable measurements for kernels A,B on a T4-equivalent node. Prototype PR opened (see design_links).

2025-11-14 - Experiment: replayed 50k production sessions in staging with KSS enabled for 5% of sessions. Observed p99 down 13% for mixed workloads; probe overhead averaged 1.6%. Need additional tuning for long-tail prompts. Added follow-up experiment to vary probe lengths.
2025-11-17 - Review feedback from SRE (Liam O'Neill): require stricter fault isolation; moved microprobe execution to preemptible lanes with timeouts. Also added telemetry for probe failures.
risks: Probe-induced jitter if not properly isolated from production lanes
Incorrect seq-len forecast can bias scouting table towards non-representative kernels
Too-frequent probes may increase cost or introduce CPU/GPU contention
Complexity in maintaining per-tenant state and ensuring consistent rollbacks across versions
test_plan: Unit tests for arch signature generation and seq-len forecast heuristics
Microbench harness tests validating timing stability across driver versions
Integration tests for scouting table persistence and TTL behavior
Staging replay: 100k-session replay experiments comparing static default vs KSS across heterogeneous fleet
Canary monitoring: per-tenant dashboards for p50/p90/p99, probe failure rate, and probe time budget utilization
notes: Trade-offs considered: full per-request search (too expensive) vs static defaults (too brittle) -> choose lightweight probing with capped budget
Open question: how aggressive should decay be when workload shifts rapidly? Default smoothing alpha=0.3 and manual override via console planned.
Follow-up: consider integrating with kernel cost-model service (ENG-772318) for cold-start predictions to reduce probe frequency
